subject: Clarify model-improvement exclusion + subprocessor evidence for ClearHealth
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@clearhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Melissa Green <melissa.green@clearhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement ask: no-training commitment + evidence of subprocessors

Hi Stephanie / Vivek,

As we move through procurement, legal has asked for explicit contractual language that prevents ClearHealth customer data from being used to improve vendor models. Specifically: 
- A clear "no training" commitment for any customer-provided prompts/responses unless we explicitly opt-in.
- Confirmation that Redwood will not claim IP over prompts or generated outputs.
- A current subprocessor registry (with locations) and any planned transfers (EU/IN/US).
- Evidence that you can provide (audit logs, attestations) showing no data was used for model training for our tenant.

Timeline: we need this by COB next Tue to stay on schedule for our security review board. Can you provide proposed DPA language and a small package of evidence? If you have any standard attestation or SOC2 control references, that would help.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Security | ClearHealth Inc

--
Attachment: procurement-questionnaire.xlsx (referenced in original procurement email)

Looping in Neha (privacy/counsel) to draft language and Vivek (CS) for the operational evidence. Quick read: ClearHealth wants a hard no-training clause and proof we haven't used their tenant data for model improvement.

My thinking (quick):
- We can agree to "No use for model training" for customer-provided content accessed via the registered Redwood account unless the customer explicitly opts in. This mirrors our hosted/private product options but needs a concise clause.
- We should offer a subprocessor registry CSV and a downloadable redacted sample of access logs (we have a standard export).
- Provide a one-page attestation signed by our security lead + pointer to SOC2 sections (CC6/CC7 equivalent) for controls around data segregation and engineering access.

Neha: can you draft the clause (plain & redlined) and call out any engineering caveats (e.g., aggregated telemetry, safety improvement signals) we must exclude or label as exceptions? Vivek: can you confirm we can produce the attached registry + redacted access log within 3 business days?

Thanks,
Steph

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement ask: no-training commitment + evidence of subprocessors

Stephanie —

Draft language attached (RDW_no-train_clause_draft.pdf). Key items and rationale:

1) No-training clause (customer content). Proposed: 
"Redwood agrees not to use Customer Content (including prompts and generated outputs) to train, fine-tune, or improve any models or model weights used by Redwood, without the Customer's prior written consent. This commitment applies to the Customer's account data and any data processed under this Agreement."

2) Limited exceptions: engineering telemetry that is wholly aggregated, de-identified, and used for system reliability may be retained. We should explicitly carve out "aggregate service metrics" and require that such telemetry contains no customer identifiers and cannot be re-associated.

3) IP / outputs: add express language that Customer retains ownership of prompts and outputs and Redwood disclaims any ownership claim over Customer outputs.

4) Evidence & attestations: We can provide: (a) subprocessor_registry_2027Q1.csv; (b) a redacted sample access_logs_sample_redacted.txt showing no model training access to tenant data; (c) a signed attestation from our Head of Security. Note: we cannot publish raw production logs; supply will be a redacted bundle over a secure drive link (see related_links).

5) Data transfers: Our subprocessor list indicates instances in US and EU data centers; we can provide SCCs/standard contractual terms for EU transfers. If ClearHealth requires data residency guarantees, escalate to Dedicated/Private deployment options.

6) Practical note for sales: this is an acceptable ask for most enterprise customers. For hosted customers who require absolute zero chance of model improvement, we should recommend Dedicated pools or Private deployment.

I'll attach a redline for the legal team. Vivek — confirm you can pull the registry + redacted logs by Tue EOD.

-Neha

Attachments: RDW_no-train_clause_draft.pdf
